notes:
Account background:
- Mid-size logistics SaaS, deterministic routing engine used in enterprise TMS customers. Low tail-latency is critical for SLA-bound customers.

Technical requirements / asks:
- Primary workload: real-time routing/chat: median latency target 40ms token-equivalent for short turn (<=128 tokens), P95 <120ms under normal load.
- Throughput: peak bursts up to 1.2k concurrent requests, steady-state ~300-400 rps.
- Needs reserved GPU pools for peak booking windows (nightly batch + daytime bursts).
- Warm pools: wants 10% warm headroom at all times, ability to pre-warm N GPU instances before peak windows.
- Autoscaling: prefer predictive scale-up (cron + workload forecasting) + reactive queue-based scale-up. Scale-down policy must avoid KV-cache thrashing; want >10min warm-to-cold threshold.
- Queueing behavior: need bounded queueing with backpressure to client; cannot accept unbounded request buffering. Prefer token-dropping for non-critical telemetry.
- Fallbacks: multi-variant routing (quantized model fallback) for graceful degradation during capacity pressure.

SLA/contract notes:
- Gyre legal pushing for 99.9% availability and P95 latency guarantee. They expect credit calculations and explicit fallback behavior documented.
- Asking Redwood to include dedicated warm pool and guaranteed ramp time in SLO table.
- Concern around disaster recovery: want cross-region warm-pool failover plan and RTO estimate.

POC/validation items requested:
- Run 72-hour soak test with mixed workload (chat + reranking) using committed instance profile. Capture P50/P90/P95 and cold-start latency distribution.
- Validate autoscaler: set conservative scale-up/down hysteresis, show queue length vs latency under synthetic spike.
- Provide tuning guide: batching config, KV cache retention tradeoffs, recommended quantization profile for cost v. quality.

Sales/ops notes & quotes:
- SE (Rina): "We saw cache churn at 5-minute cooldown in our lab; moving to 15-minute appears acceptable."
- AE (Ethan): "Priority: predictable tail latency during booking spikes — customers will churn if routing calls slow down."

Next steps (short):
- Send updated sizing workbook with warm pool + DR addendum (by 2024-12-22).
- Legal to review SLA addendum (Gyre legal + Redwood legal sync week of 2024-12-30).
- Schedule 72-hour soak for mid-Jan (POC kickoff).
